encounters.cc: Worsening fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and dry cough over 8 months with unintentional weight loss

lines: Worsening fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and dry cough over 8 months with unintentional weight loss
He has difficulty walking up a flight of stairs without stopping to catch his breath.
He reports a persistent dry cough and a 4-kg unintentional weight loss during this time.
- Stage IIIB non-small cell lung cancer
- Pending elective left inguinal hernia repair
- Albuterol 90 mcg inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath
- Father: Lung cancer diagnosed at age 72
He has a 50-pack-year smoking history and worked as a construction foreman until retirement 3 years ago.
He denies wheezing, chest tightness, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
His temperature is 36.7°C (98.1°F), pulse is 84/min, respiratory rate is 20/min, and oxygen saturation is 91% on room air.
Lung examination reveals fine, dry bibasilar crackles and digital clubbing.
Chest x-ray reveals a decreased lung volume with reticular markings predominantly in the lower lobes.
High-resolution CT reveals subpleural and basilar-predominant honeycombing and reticulations.
Pulmonary function testing shows reduced total lung capacity, decreased diffusion capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO), and a preserved FEV1/FVC ratio.
Despite poor lung compliance and low oxygenation, he is found to have no evidence of dynamic airway collapse on spirometry or imaging.
The patient is started on antifibrotic therapy and referred for lung transplant evaluation.
